stories.title: Protect persistent citizen identity across save/load
stories.i_want: every citizen's identity and personal state to survive a save/load cycle unchanged
stories.so_that: I can follow a specific person across sessions instead of a respawned, fungible population

acceptance_criteria.text: Saving then loading the simulation reproduces every HumanEnt's PersonalInfo fields byte-identical to the pre-save state. [SUBSTRATE: PROVIDED — souls/human.rs PersonalInfo in HumanEnt, whole sim serialized via CompressedBincode]

Two citizens with identical attribute values (age, education, etc.) remain distinguishable by stable entity/soul reference after a reload — souls are not fungible. [SUBSTRATE: PROVIDED — HumanEnt entity identity via ECS, egregoria-substrate-audit.md sec.5]

stories.title: Protect fixed workplace binding
stories.i_want: a citizen's assigned workplace to stay a stable single reference until an explicit reassignment event
stories.so_that: labour allocation stays plannable instead of reshuffling itself every tick

acceptance_criteria.text: A citizen's Work.workplace value does not change absent an explicit reassignment event (job loss, workplace destroyed, plan reassignment). [SUBSTRATE: PROVIDED — souls/desire/work.rs:20-26]
The workplace binding persists unchanged across a save/load cycle. [SUBSTRATE: PROVIDED — souls/human.rs HumanEnt via CompressedBincode]

stories.title: Protect purchase settlement on physical arrival, not on trade match
stories.i_want: shop stock to debit and a buyer's goods to credit only when the buyer physically arrives at the shop
stories.so_that: the CS1 teleport-credit exploit (goods appearing before the trip completes) cannot return as a regression

acceptance_criteria.text: When a buy order is matched but the citizen has not yet arrived at the shop, neither shop stock nor citizen/household inventory changes. [SUBSTRATE: PROVIDED — souls/desire/buyfood.rs:50-54, the spec's target bug is already fixed]
Stock debit and buyer credit occur atomically at the tick of physical arrival, not at the tick the trade was matched. [SUBSTRATE: PROVIDED — souls/desire/buyfood.rs:50-54]

stories.title: Model per-citizen need satisfaction beyond food
stories.i_want: each citizen to track 0..1 satisfaction across warmth, water, health, housing space/quality and rest, not only food
stories.so_that: shortages other than hunger become visible economic signals instead of invisible gaps

acceptance_criteria.text: A CitizenNeeds structure exists with distinct 0..1 fields for food, warmth, water, health, housingSpace, housingQuality and rest. [SUBSTRATE: ABSENT — greenfield; today only three score() functions (Home constant 0.2, Work binary window, BuyFood hunger clock) exist in souls/human.rs:190-231, no CitizenNeeds struct]

Each need decays over simulated time and refills only on a real satisfying event (goods delivered, or a trip to a stocked/staffed building), never by ambient coverage. [SUBSTRATE: ABSENT — greenfield]

Wants (consumer goods, culture, leisure) and aspirations (car, bigger flat, education) are tracked as a separate slower-updating layer whose chronic pressure can cross a threshold and become economic demand. [SUBSTRATE: ABSENT — greenfield, OURS per spec/needs.md]

A loyalty/political-legitimacy meta-need is tracked as a satisfaction-driven aggregate distinct from the per-citizen needs/wants/aspirations fields, moved by broadcast/propaganda and monument-style sources. [SUBSTRATE: ABSENT — greenfield, W&R $MONUMENT_GOVERNMENT_LOYALTY per spec/needs.md:67]

The wants layer has named fields (goods, alcohol, culture, sport, spiritual, recreation) and each field's satisfaction is spatial and quality-weighted: pollution near the serving building lowers it, nature/water proximity raises it. [SUBSTRATE: ABSENT — greenfield, W&R $ATTRACTIVE_FACTOR_* per spec/needs.md:30-36,72-75]

Durable needs (housing, appliances, car) resolve and are tracked at household level, while consumable needs (food, health, education) resolve and are tracked at individual-citizen level. [SUBSTRATE: ABSENT — greenfield per spec/needs.md:82 open-question resolution]

Needs recompute on the simulation clock's low-frequency band while aspirations recompute on the distinctly slower very-low (months) band; an aspiration's pressure value does not change on a tick where only the needs band fired. [SUBSTRATE: ABSENT — greenfield, architecture/simulation-clock.md per spec/needs.md:79]

stories.title: Introduce households as shared-pantry family units
stories.i_want: citizens grouped into household entities that share a single dwelling and a single pantry
stories.so_that: housing allocation and shopping demand are computed at the family level, not artificially per-person

acceptance_criteria.text: A Household entity groups member citizens under one dwellingRef and one shared pantry buffer, capped at an authored constant (not hardcoded to CS1's fixed value of 5) so the cap can be tuned without a code change. [SUBSTRATE: ABSENT — greenfield; every human currently owns its own home and its own pantry, no Household entity exists; cap value is an open question per spec/households.md:65]
Consumption by any household member debits the shared household pantry, not a private per-citizen stock. [SUBSTRATE: ABSENT — greenfield]
A dwellingRef of zero represents a household with no assigned flat (in the housing queue), distinct from an assigned dwelling. [SUBSTRATE: ABSENT — greenfield]

A new household pantry starts at 200, drains 20 per step from consumption, and triggers a shopping trip once it falls below 200, refilling by 100 per completed trip. [SUBSTRATE: ABSENT — greenfield, CS1 CONFIRMED constants per spec/households.md:34]

stories.title: Allocate housing through an explicit, player-visible queue
stories.i_want: unhoused households to sit in a policy-weighted, visible queue rather than being matched invisibly or deleted
stories.so_that: housing shortage is a legible planning failure, not a silent population loss

acceptance_criteria.text: A household with no vacancy assigned enters a queue ranked by policy weights (priority class, workplace proximity, family-size-to-flat-size fit); queue length is a value the player can read, and no dwelling or household carries a price/affordability field of any kind — queue position, never money, gates assignment. [SUBSTRATE: ABSENT — greenfield, OURS per spec/households.md; CS1's equivalent is an invisible priority x distance market, no visible queue exists; spec/households.md:16 'No RCI bar']

A household displaced by building loss or eviction re-enters the queue; it is never deleted from the simulation for lack of housing. [SUBSTRATE: ABSENT — greenfield; explicitly rejects CS1's ResidentAI.cs:2434-2445 citizen-deletion pattern per spec/households.md evidence log]

Overcrowding (two households doubled into one flat) is a representable, distinguishable state from a normally-assigned flat. [SUBSTRATE: ABSENT — greenfield; capacity is authored as flats x max_household_size specifically to make overcrowding representable]

stories.title: Replace distance-only job matching with planner-directed, tier-and-commute-aware allocation
stories.i_want: job assignment to respect minimum education tier and commute feasibility, not just proximity
stories.so_that: labour allocation is a plannable resource rather than a euclidean-distance market trade

acceptance_criteria.text: A vacancy is only filled by a citizen who meets the slot's minimum education tier. [SUBSTRATE: CONFLICTS — today a job vacancy is literally traded as ItemID::new("job-opening") matched purely by squared Euclidean distance, souls/human.rs:267-269 and economy/market.rs:216, with no education check at all]

A candidate whose commute time (or distance under an authored feasibility threshold) exceeds the allocator's limit is not assigned to that vacancy even if no closer candidate exists. [SUBSTRATE: CONFLICTS — no commute feasibility check exists in the current distance-ranked trade, market.rs:216-219]

Commute trips are timed by a time-of-day probability curve rather than a uniform/random departure time, matching the CS1 commute-timing shape. [SUBSTRATE: ABSENT — greenfield, CS1 CONFIRMED shape per spec/citizens.md:65]

stories.title: Model health, sickness and hospital-capacity resolution
stories.i_want: citizen health to be derived from physical service inputs and sickness to be a resolvable service event
stories.so_that: neglecting people (no water/sewage/care coverage) physically reduces output through a legible causal chain

acceptance_criteria.text: Citizen health recomputes from physical inputs only (water/sewage access, pollution, garbage, care coverage vs. age-phase requirement) — money never appears in the calculation. [SUBSTRATE: ABSENT — greenfield; HumanEnt has no health or wellbeing field today, only age set once at spawn]
A sustained low-health streak triggers a sickness roll; a sick citizen posts a hospital-transport need whose resolution consumes hospital capacity. [SUBSTRATE: ABSENT — greenfield]
While sick, a citizen's economic life (work attendance, shopping trips) is frozen until the sickness resolves. [SUBSTRATE: ABSENT — greenfield]

A citizen's work efficiency scales continuously across the 10-100% range as a function of health, not as a binary sick/not-sick cutoff. [SUBSTRATE: ABSENT — greenfield, CS1 CONFIRMED table `workEfficiency(health)` per spec/citizens.md:61]

stories.title: Progress citizen age and introduce death without deleting the household
stories.i_want: citizen age to advance over simulated time and citizens to die within a widened age window, freeing a household slot rather than dissolving the household
stories.so_that: the population has a real demographic lifecycle instead of a frozen age field

acceptance_criteria.text: A citizen's age field increases as simulated time passes. [SUBSTRATE: ABSENT — greenfield; age is set once at spawn and never incremented, per egregoria-substrate-audit.md sec.5]
Death occurs by an age window widened by poor health and a small accident chance; on death the citizen's household persists with the slot freed, not dissolved. [SUBSTRATE: ABSENT — greenfield]

Population aging or decline never halts or ends the simulation — it only produces a visible demographic strain signal, consistent with the project's no-game-over principle. [SUBSTRATE: ABSENT — greenfield; no death/lifecycle exists today so no failure-mode behaviour to regress against]

A citizen transitions through coarse lifecycle stages (child -> student -> worker -> pensioner) at named age thresholds, gaining/losing school- and job-eligibility at each transition, rather than a fixed life-stage that never changes as age increases. [SUBSTRATE: ABSENT — greenfield, CS1 shape (AgeGroup thresholds a la 15/45/90/180/240) per spec/citizens.md:32,70]

stories.title: Make unmet needs legible: wait, substitute, or visibly go without
stories.i_want: a citizen whose need cannot currently be met to show a visible queuing or going-without state, rather than an order that silently sits unmatched
stories.so_that: shortage is felt and actionable — a longer queue or going without, never an invisible stall or a game-over

acceptance_criteria.text: An unmatched buy order surfaces the citizen in an observable waiting/queued state rather than the order sitting with no player-visible signal. [SUBSTRATE: ABSENT — greenfield; there is no wait/substitute/go-without state machine, an unmatched buy order just sits, economy/market.rs]

Wait-time urgency reuses the elapsed-since-last-satisfied clock already computed for hunger as its felt-urgency signal. [SUBSTRATE: PARTIAL — souls/human.rs:190-231, BuyFood::score already computes urgency from elapsed time since last eating, ready-made hook per audit sec.5]

When urgency crosses a threshold and no substitute good/building is available, the citizen enters an observable 'going without' state rather than despawning, error-looping, or waiting silently forever. [SUBSTRATE: ABSENT — greenfield]

stories.title: Keep the per-citizen decision loop performant as population grows
stories.i_want: citizen decision-making to preserve its per-human staggering and stay within a measured tick budget as headcount rises
stories.so_that: the game remains playable at realistic city population sizes instead of degrading unnoticed

acceptance_criteria.text: Each human's re-decision interval remains a randomized 30-80 tick stagger, spatially seeded, so the population is not all re-evaluated on the same tick. [SUBSTRATE: PROVIDED — souls/human.rs:185, 30 + rand2(pos)*50 ticks]

A profiled population ceiling exists and is documented — full-human-collection update time per tick stays under a stated frame budget at that ceiling. [SUBSTRATE: UNAUDITED — population ceiling is UNCONFIRMED per egregoria-substrate-audit.md sec.5/sec.9, needs runtime profiling, not a code read]

stories.title: Grow the population through household birth
stories.i_want: eligible couples with a free household slot to have a per-step chance of a birth, boosted by childcare access
stories.so_that: population growth is a real demographic event coupled to service coverage, not a fixed/absent counter

acceptance_criteria.text: A birth can occur only when a household has a present couple, both adults, and a free member slot; a household missing any of these three preconditions never produces a birth. [SUBSTRATE: ABSENT — greenfield, CS1 CONFIRMED birth gate per spec/households.md:54]

The per-step birth chance rises from a baseline of 1/12 to 1/8 when the household has childcare access, so improving childcare coverage measurably raises the observed birth rate. [SUBSTRATE: ABSENT — greenfield, CS1 CONFIRMED constants per spec/households.md:54]

stories.title: Allocate student seats through a capacity-limited education pipeline
stories.i_want: a student seat to be a planned, capacity-limited allocation like a job vacancy, throttled by per-tier throughput
stories.so_that: education is a physical pipeline with real trade-offs against labour, not ambient coverage that grants diplomas for free

acceptance_criteria.text: A student is assigned a school seat through the same planned-allocation mechanism as a job vacancy (using workBuilding + a Student flag), unifying commute and capacity accounting between work and study. [SUBSTRATE: ABSENT — greenfield, CS1's SetStudentplace trick, CONFIRMED per spec/citizens.md:51]

Each education tier enforces an attended-capacity throughput ceiling (kindergarten 10, school 12, university 3); a citizen cannot occupy a seat beyond the tier's authored throughput. [SUBSTRATE: ABSENT — greenfield, W&R $CITIZEN_ABLE_SERVE CONFIRMED per spec/citizens.md:52]

A citizen with no attended school/university seat never gains the associated education-tier credential, rejecting CS1's ambient education field where coverage alone grants diplomas. [SUBSTRATE: ABSENT — greenfield; explicitly rejects CS1's ResidentAI.cs:1259-1330 ambient-coverage pattern per spec/citizens.md:52]

stories.title: Dispatch surge labour via a labour-pool office without touching fixed bindings
stories.i_want: unassigned or temporary workers to be dispatchable to short-lived demands (construction, harvest) through a labour-pool office
stories.so_that: surge work gets staffed without disturbing any citizen's fixed Work.workplace binding

acceptance_criteria.text: The labour-pool office dispatches unassigned/temporary workers to a short-lived demand (e.g. a construction site) and, after the demand ends, every dispatched citizen's fixed Work.workplace value is unchanged from before the dispatch. [SUBSTRATE: ABSENT — greenfield, W&R $RESOURCE_SOURCE_WORKERS CONFIRMED, kept as the one W&R pattern per spec/citizens.md:47]

stories.title: Author dwelling quality and default-on service requirements
stories.i_want: each dwelling prefab to carry an authored qualityOfLiving scalar and to require heat/electricity by default
stories.so_that: housing quality feeds citizen satisfaction and no residential building can silently opt out of basic services

acceptance_criteria.text: Each dwelling prefab carries an authored qualityOfLiving scalar in the observed CONFIRMED range (0.60 khrushchyovka to 1.02 village house), and this value feeds a household member's housingQuality need. [SUBSTRATE: ABSENT — greenfield, W&R CONFIRMED range per spec/households.md:48]

A residential building requires heat and electricity by default (no dwelling prefab declares a heating/electricity opt-out); only a non-residential prefab may opt out via an explicit disable flag. [SUBSTRATE: ABSENT — greenfield, W&R CONFIRMED-by-absence per spec/households.md:48]

stories.title: Couple wellbeing to work attendance and crime propensity
stories.epic_theme: Crime — deviance and the justice chain
stories.i_want: a citizen's wellbeing to cost them when filling a below-tier slot, and sustained low wellbeing to raise crime propensity and lower work attendance
stories.so_that: wellbeing is a plannable lever on both labour supply and crime, not a cosmetic stat

acceptance_criteria.text: An overqualified citizen may fill a lower-tier slot but a lower-tier citizen is never assigned above their tier; filling below tier costs the citizen wellbeing. [SUBSTRATE: ABSENT — greenfield; no wellbeing field or overqualification cascade exists on HumanEnt today]

A citizen's work-attendance probability scales continuously with wellbeing (workProbability(wellbeing)), and sustained low wellbeing raises that citizen's contribution to the crime rate, mirroring the CS1 GetCrimeRate/GetWorkProbability coupling. [SUBSTRATE: ABSENT — greenfield; no wellbeing-driven crime or attendance-probability coupling exists today, CS1 CONFIRMED per spec/needs.md:65]

scenarios.title: Save/load roundtrip preserves citizen identity
preconditions: Running simulation with N citizens having distinct PersonalInfo values

steps.action: Serialize the simulation to a save
expected: Save completes without error

steps.action: Deserialize the save into a fresh simulation
expected: Human count matches pre-save count

steps.action: Compare each loaded HumanEnt's PersonalInfo against its pre-save counterpart
expected: Every field is byte-identical
entity-to-soul mapping is unchanged

final_observables: No citizen's identity fields differ from before the save
owning_story_titles: Protect persistent citizen identity across save/load

scenarios.title: Determinism replay detects accidental citizen-state divergence
preconditions: TestCtx harness available, per simulation/src/tests/mod.rs

steps.action: Run a recorded session twice independently through TestCtx::tick
expected: Both runs round-trip through bincode each tick

steps.action: Hash-compare per-tick state between the two runs
expected: Hashes match at every tick, including citizen fields

final_observables: No divergence tick is found for citizen-related state
owning_story_titles: Protect persistent citizen identity across save/load

scenarios.title: Workplace binding survives a full workday cycle without silent reassignment
preconditions: A citizen with an assigned Work.workplace
No reassignment event triggered

steps.action: Advance the simulation through a full day/night cycle
expected: Citizen commutes to and from the same workplace

steps.action: Read Work.workplace after the cycle
expected: Value is unchanged from the start of the cycle

final_observables: Work.workplace equals its pre-cycle value
owning_story_titles: Protect fixed workplace binding

scenarios.title: Buy order match does not move goods before physical arrival
preconditions: A citizen's buy order has been matched to a seller
Citizen has not yet reached the shop

steps.action: Advance ticks up to but not including the arrival tick
expected: Shop stock is unchanged
Citizen/household inventory is unchanged

steps.action: Advance to the arrival tick
expected: Shop stock debits by the traded amount
Citizen/household inventory credits by the traded amount, in the same tick

final_observables: No goods movement occurred before physical arrival; movement is atomic on arrival
owning_story_titles: Protect purchase settlement on physical arrival, not on trade match

scenarios.title: Household pantry is shared, not per-member

expected: The single household pantry level drops by the combined draw of all members

steps.action: Inspect any individual member's inventory
expected: No member holds a private food stock separate from the household pantry

final_observables: Pantry level reflects combined household consumption, never a per-citizen stock

scenarios.title: Housing queue grows visibly when no vacancy exists

expected: A new household is created with dwellingRef = 0

expected: Queue length increments by one

final_observables: The new household appears in the queue and is not silently dropped or auto-housed

scenarios.title: Eviction returns a household to the queue instead of deleting it
preconditions: A housed household occupies a flat that is condemned/destroyed

steps.action: Trigger the building-loss event
expected: Household dwellingRef resets to 0

steps.action: Check the simulation's household count and the queue
expected: Household count is unchanged (no deletion)
The household appears in the housing queue

final_observables: The displaced household is present in the queue with all members intact

scenarios.title: Job assignment respects minimum education tier over raw proximity
preconditions: Two open vacancies: a near tier-0 slot and a far tier-1 slot
One candidate citizen who meets only the tier-1 minimum education requirement

steps.action: Run the labour allocation pass for the candidate
expected: Candidate is not assigned to the near tier-0 slot despite shorter distance

steps.action: Check the far tier-1 slot
expected: Candidate is assigned there if it also satisfies commute feasibility

final_observables: Assignment outcome is governed by education-tier eligibility, not distance alone

scenarios.title: Sick citizen's economic activity freezes until hospital capacity resolves it
preconditions: A citizen has sustained a low-health streak and rolled sick
A hospital-transport need has been posted

steps.action: Advance ticks while hospital capacity is unavailable
expected: Citizen does not commute to work
Citizen does not execute shopping trips

steps.action: Free hospital capacity and let the need resolve
expected: Sickness clears
Work/shopping behaviour resumes on the next eligible decision tick

final_observables: No economic activity is recorded for the citizen during the sick window; activity resumes only after resolution
owning_story_titles: Model health, sickness and hospital-capacity resolution

scenarios.title: Citizen death frees a household slot without dissolving the household
preconditions: A household with a member near the upper end of the death age window and poor health

steps.action: Advance ticks until the death condition triggers
expected: Member is removed from the simulation

steps.action: Inspect the household afterward
expected: Household entity still exists
Remaining members are unaffected
The freed member slot is available for a future member

final_observables: Household persists post-death with one fewer member and no cascading deletion
owning_story_titles: Progress citizen age and introduce death without deleting the household

scenarios.title: Unmet need surfaces as a visible waiting or going-without state
preconditions: A citizen's buy order cannot currently be matched (no seller/stock available)

steps.action: Advance ticks while the order remains unmatched
expected: The citizen is shown in a queued/waiting state to the player
Felt urgency rises using the elapsed-since-satisfied clock

steps.action: Continue advancing until urgency crosses the going-without threshold with no substitute available
expected: Citizen enters an observable going-without state, distinct from queued-waiting

final_observables: At every tick the citizen's need state (satisfied / waiting / going-without) is player-observable, never a silent unmatched order
owning_story_titles: Make unmet needs legible: wait, substitute, or visibly go without

scenarios.title: Full-population tick time stays within budget at the profiled ceiling

expected: Duration stays under budget for the sampled ticks

scenarios.title: Childcare access raises the observed birth rate

scenarios.title: Work efficiency scales continuously with health

expected: The short-commute citizen's rest satisfaction recovers faster or higher than the long-commute citizen's

final_observables: Rest satisfaction is coupled to commute length, not a flat schedule-only refill
owning_story_titles: Model per-citizen need satisfaction beyond food

scenarios.title: Dwelling quality and default heat/electricity requirement feed housing need and reject silent opt-out
preconditions: Two dwelling prefabs with different authored qualityOfLiving values
A residential prefab with no heating/electricity declaration

steps.action: House equivalent households in each dwelling prefab
